clue.text: October 1920

parts.note: read as a birth date: the American film actor of The Odd Couple was born on 1 October 1920

explanation.walkthrough: One of four clues in this puzzle that give nothing but a birth date; the others are SHANKAR, BUKOWSKI and LENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue names only the month and year of a famous person's birth, so the solver must find the comic Hollywood actor born then.

clue.text: Swift passage, timely, about Lilliputian

definitions.meaning: a sixtieth of an hour, a short span of time that passes quickly
tiny, like the little people of Lilliput in Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A literary critic remarks on a well-timed passage of Swift's about the Lilliputians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' suggests Jonathan Swift, who invented Lilliput, but in the first definition it just means quick; 'about' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliputian is a byword for very small, a synonym of tiny; a swift passage of time can be a sixty-second span.

clue.text: Several artful line drawings of his illustrated wonderful creatures

definitions.text: drawings of his illustrated wonderful creatures

parts.note: ten taken as a loose stand-in for several, a handful of things

indicators.note: artful means cleverly contrived, so the letters of line are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist's few clever pen strokes depicted marvellous beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artful' turns LINE into NIEL. The 'wonderful creatures' are those of Alice in Wonderland, which John Tenniel illustrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Tenniel drew the original pictures for Lewis Carroll's Alice books, peopled with Wonderland creatures.

clue.text: Nine of eight perhaps, the time after sunset

definitions.meaning: in this grid the entry at 8 is NINETIES, and its first four letters, NINE, make up half of that grid entry

explanation.surface: Someone asks what nine out of eight might be, then turns to the hour after sunset.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'light' is a crossword entry: the word NINE fills half of the eight-letter light at 8-down, so it is a half of a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight, the dim glow after sunset, is commonly called the half-light.

clue.text: Shun cuddle perhaps about start of elopement? Not planned!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
perhaps suggests the words shun and cuddle may be some other arrangement of their letters
start of picks the opening letter of the word elopement

explanation.surface: An eloping couple avoid an embrace, and the whole escapade was spur of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal; 'about' puts the shuffled ten letters round the 'start of elopement'. The eloping couple is surface colour only.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unscheduled happens without being arranged in advance, a synonym of unplanned.

clue.text: Philosopher's reason for going or not going?) to a Viennese concert?

definitions.meaning: the French thinker Henri, author of Creative Evolution

definitions.text: reason for going or not going?) to a Viennese concert?
definitions.meaning: the Viennese composer Alban Berg is on the programme, a reason to attend or to stay away

explanation.surface: Someone muses on why a thinker would or would not go to a concert in Vienna.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the answer as BERG'S ON. Whether a programme of Berg's atonal music draws you in or keeps you away depends on taste. The stray bracket is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Bergson was a French philosopher of time and intuition and Nobel laureate in literature.

clue.text: One is into Schubert's 5th and 1st. Encore!

indicators.note: into says the numeral goes inside the letters that follow
5th picks the fifth letter of Schubert's name
1st picks the opening letter of the same name

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A music lover, into Schubert's Fifth and First Symphonies, shouts for more.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifth and first letters of 'Schubert' are B and S; 'into' puts I (one) between them. 'Schubert's 5th' looks like the symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Bis is the cry for a repeat performance used in French and Italian concert halls, the same as calling for an encore.

clue.text: Verse form upsets one with a rhotacism

indicators.note: in a down entry upsets means the letters are turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a rhotacism is an unusual r sound, such as the rolled or uvular burr, also spelt bur

explanation.surface: A form of poetry somehow unsettles a reader with a speech defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' turns I + A + BUR into RUBAI. A burr (also spelt bur) is a rough, throaty r sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubai is a Persian quatrain, the stanza of Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat.

clue.text: April 1920

parts.note: read as a birth date: the Indian sitar virtuoso was born on 7 April 1920

explanation.walkthrough: One of four birth-date clues in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue gives only the month and year of birth, so the solver must find the famous sitar player born then.

clue.text: Which represents one intense period during which His Dark Materials was written

definitions.text: period during which His Dark Materials was written

indicators.note: represents is read as re-presents, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A reader recalls the intense stretch in which Pullman wrote his trilogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represents' rearranges I + INTENSE. Philip Pullman's His Dark Materials trilogy came out from 1995 to 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: Pullman wrote the trilogy in the last decade of the twentieth century, the decade of the 1990s.

clue.text: Perplexes by deducting marks?

definitions.meaning: read as taking away plus signs, the pluses being marks

explanation.surface: An examiner baffles students by docking points.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as NON-PLUSES, removing plus marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle or bewilder them, a synonym of perplex.

clue.text: It's leaving Britain, making Deighton's worth a billion

indicators.note: leaving says the two letters depart from the word Britain

parts.note: the word it, with the possessive giving no letters

explanation.surface: Something exits the UK and, with Deighton, makes a billion.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IT out of BRITAIN. Len Deighton's spy novel is Billion-Dollar Brain, so the brain is 'worth a billion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deighton's novel title gives the organ worth a billion dollars, the cerebral mind of the story.

clue.text: Examination on Kafka

definitions.meaning: a test or hearing in court
Franz Kafka's novel, Der Process in German, about Josef K's prosecution

explanation.surface: A test paper on Kafka's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test or a court hearing, and The Trial is Kafka's best-known novel.

clue.text: One way to get out from a gate after strike action

indicators.note: after places the gate piece behind the blow

parts.note: the act of striking, a blow
a wicket is a small gate or door, as in a wicket gate

explanation.surface: Industrial action has workers leaving through a gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike action' looks like a walkout by workers. In cricket a batter is out hit wicket by knocking over their own stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit wicket is one of the ways a cricket batter can be dismissed, by breaking their own stumps.

clue.text: Ford is a farcical playwright that's skilful

definitions.note: loosely, what can be forded can be crossed; the clue word is a noun or verb, the answer an adjective

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces such as Rookery Nook
skilful means able, capable

explanation.surface: A writer named Ford is called a skilled author of farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like the novelist Ford Madox Ford. Ben Travers was a British writer of 1920s stage farces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ford is a river crossing, and a fordable river is one that can be crossed on foot, so passable.

clue.text: Waste time with Hades and oread playing around after sport's over

indicators.note: after places the mixed letters behind the reversed sport
over means turned over, so the word for the sport is read backwards

parts.note: golf is a sport; the possessive gives no letters

indicators.note: playing around means the letters frolic into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain nymph and the god of the underworld fool about once a game has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing around' is the anagram signal for the nymph and the god; 'over' turns the sport backwards, and 'after' sets the anagram behind it. An oread is a mountain nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog a dead horse is an idiom for wasting effort on a lost cause.

clue.text: In which a pop song may have to run the gauntlet?

definitions.text: In which a pop song may have to run the gauntlet?

parts.words: In which a pop song may have to run the gauntlet?
parts.note: running the gauntlet means walking between rows of people being struck, so picture a procession of blows a song must pass through

explanation.walkthrough: Running the gauntlet means being beaten while passing between two lines of people: a parade of blows, hence the pop chart's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly pop chart is a ranking a song must survive, the place where records are listed by sales.

clue.text: August 1920

parts.note: read as a birth date: the German-born American poet of Los Angeles low life was born on 16 August 1920

explanation.walkthrough: One of four birth-date clues in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue gives only the month and year of birth, so the solver must find the hard-living poet and novelist born then.

clue.text: "My muse had wings … Whither I bent her force, —— yet divine to me" (Keats)

definitions.text: "My muse had wings … Whither I bent her force, —— yet divine to me" (Keats)

parts.words: "My muse had wings … Whither I bent her force, —— yet divine to me" (Keats)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing: the dash stands for a single adjective in the Keats poem

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Keats's verse epistle To My Brother George: the solver supplies the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is from Keats's early epistle, describing his muse as lacking intellect yet still divine to him.

clue.text: Amin, quickly returning, supposedly like Prince Myshkin

parts.note: Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator

indicators.note: returning means the Latin word is read backwards

parts.note: cito is Latin for quickly, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: The dictator hurries back, said to resemble a Dostoevsky prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CITO into OTIC. Prince Myshkin is the hero of Dostoevsky's The Idiot, hence 'supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Myshkin is the title character of The Idiot, so to be like him is, by reputation, foolish.

clue.text: Bad Cockney actor or the most eminent? Betjeman's was Cockney

parts.note: a bad actor is a ham, and a Cockney drops the initial h
the most eminent is first, written 1st, which looks like the letters IST

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether a Cockney actor is awful or the greatest, noting Betjeman's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the most eminent' is 1ST, read as letters. Betjeman wrote a poem called The Cockney Amorist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Betjeman's poem The Cockney Amorist is about a Londoner in love, a lover by temperament.

clue.text: Academician deserting trainee lyricist

indicators.note: deserting means the academician's letter leaves the word

parts.note: a learner, as on L-plates
A is an abbreviation for academician, as in ARA

explanation.surface: A member of the academy walks out on a student songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Jay Lerner wrote the words for My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerner wrote the lyrics for Broadway musicals such as Camelot, so he was a songwriter of words.

clue.text: One heartlessly corrupted ladies about start of lechery. Wink wink!

indicators.note: heartlessly means the word one loses its middle letter
about means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
corrupted means the letters of ladies are spoilt into a new order
start of picks the opening letter of lechery

explanation.surface: A heartless rake leads women astray in a spell of lust, nudge nudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves OE; 'corrupted' shuffles LADIES, which goes 'about' L, the start of 'lechery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeillades are amorous glances or knowing winks, from the French for an eye-look.

clue.text: April 1870

parts.note: read as a birth date: the Bolshevik leader was born on 22 April 1870

explanation.walkthrough: One of four birth-date clues in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue gives only the month and year of birth, so the solver must find the Russian revolutionary born then.

clue.text: Like Titus, one at heart of trilogy at Peake's ending

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a

indicators.note: heart of picks the middle letter of the seven-letter word trilogy

parts.note: at and on can both mean in position, as in on time

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of Peake's name

explanation.surface: Mervyn Peake's hero stands at the centre of a trilogy as it closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Alone is the third book of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast trilogy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peake titled the trilogy's last book Titus Alone, so Titus there is solitary.

clue.text: One described by Milton at a stroke being overthrown

indicators.note: being overthrown says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Milton portrays a figure toppled with a single blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NATAS sits across 'Milton at a', read backwards. Milton's Satan is hurled from Heaven in Paradise Lost, apt for 'overthrown'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fallen angel is the figure Milton portrays in Paradise Lost, his best-known character.

clue.text: Larkin, for example, on balance mostly a heretic

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales
an Arian follows Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: The poet Larkin is judged, all things considered, largely a dissenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LIBRA to LIBR. Philip Larkin ran the library at Hull University for thirty years.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin worked as a university librarian, so he is an instance of a library keeper.

clue.text: Subject of Poe's somewhat facile elegy?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words facile elegy is taken

explanation.surface: A critic finds Poe's lament for his subject rather glib.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe's last poem, Annabel Lee, mourns a lost bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel Lee is the title figure of Poe's poem, the woman whose death it laments.

clue.text: Popular scene recreated that involves myrrh for instance

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: recreated means the letters of scene are made again in another order

explanation.surface: A popular nativity tableau is re-staged with the gift of myrrh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreated' shuffles SCENE into CENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrrh is an aromatic resin burned for its fragrant smoke, an example of perfumed offering.

clue.text: Hanoverian who's making one cross?

definitions.meaning: the Prince-... of Hanover, a prince with a vote for Holy Roman Emperor
a voter marks a ballot paper with an X

explanation.surface: A Hanoverian prince asks who is annoying someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; here it is the X on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of Hanover held the title Elector, and anyone who votes in an election marks a ballot.
